From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Pilot Plan & Next Steps — Kalima Systems (post-call recap)

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for the 45-minute discovery today. Quick recap and proposed pilot plan so we have alignment before I loop in the engineering kickoff: 

Key pain points you shared
- Legacy ETL is introducing 12–18s end-to-end response times for customer-facing summarization flows; conversions drop ~15% on long threads.
- Current on-prem model is expensive to operate for spikes and lacks prompt-level monitoring for quality regressions.
- Security: SSO + SCIM and audit logs are mandatory for any PII flows.

Primary objectives for the pilot
1) Reduce mean response time for the summarization endpoint to <= 800ms and p95 <= 1500ms under typical load.
2) Maintain or improve summary quality vs. current baseline (we'll use a 20-prompt eval set and judge on F1/relevance).
3) Validate cost per 1k tokens run-rate with Redwood Optimize suggestions (target: 30% lower token cost than current inferencing).

Proposed scope (Pilot Lite — 4 weeks)
- Week 0 (access/setup): service account provisioning, SSO test user, dataset ingestion (5k sample threads).
- Week 1: baseline profiling (latency/cost) on your sample dataset; initial prompt set experiments (10 prompts).
- Week 2: quantization + batching config tuning; run evaluation suite (20 prompts) and produce quality delta report.
- Week 3: final performance run, cost projection, and recommendations for production rollout.

Owners/roles
- Kalima: Aisha (product lead) | Samir (platform/infra).
- Redwood: Neha (eng-sponsor / customer success), Priyom (solutions engineer — access & dataset upload), Rishi (runtime lead — performance tuning).

Access / setup checklist (what we need from Kalima to start)
1) A test SSO user or temporary SAML credentials (low-risk account) — see attached kalima-sso-setup.md.
2) Short export of 5k representative threads (anonymized) or S3 access to a staging bucket.
3) Confirmation on the evaluation rubric: acceptable tradeoffs between terseness vs. factuality (we suggested relevance-weighted F1 + human pass/fail).

Deliverables
- Pilot scope doc (attached: pilot-scope-v1.pdf)
- Weekly status with latency/cost dashboards and prompt evals
- Final recommendations and a production runbook if the pilot meets SLOs.

Next steps (action items)
- Aisha: confirm you can share SSO test credentials and dataset by EOD Monday (Dec 8).
- Samir: procurement contact to confirm NDA/PO path — cc procurement@waltercorp.com if needed.
- Priyom/Rishi: we’ll prepare an onboarding playbook and a lightweight infra checklist.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-minute engineering kickoff next Wednesday (Dec 9) and invite Kalima platform + our runtime lead.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: kalima-sso-setup.md (text)]

Neha — thanks for the thorough recap. This mirrors what we heard internally. A few clarifications and confirmations: 

- Dataset: we can export a 5k anonymized sample by Monday morning to an S3 staging bucket and will share credentials with Priyom.
- SSO: Samir will provision a test SAML user and we will send the metadata.
- Evaluation rubric: we agree to the relevance-weighted F1 + human pass/fail. We'll add a short customer-facing readability check that matters to product.

Procurement note: procurement@kalima-systems.com will need a Statement of Work before any paid engagement. I copied them on a separate thread; they requested estimated cost bands. Can you provide a one-page Ballpark estimate for the Pilot Lite (engineering hours + infra credits)?

We are good to go for the Wednesday kickoff if you can get the invite out. 

Thanks,
Aisha
